LESSON: WHOLE NUMBERS (10

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.1: Whole Numbers (10

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Whole Numbers (10. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: What should you consider when writing numbersin words?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use place value and total value of digits up to tens of thousands in daily life situations,
2. read and write numbers up to 10,000 in symbols in real-life situations,
3. read and write numbers up to 1,000 in words in day-to-day activities,

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market in your county, count 10 mangoes. Put them in 2 groups of 5. That is sorting and grouping.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row. Write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and your parent gives you 5 more, you have 12 shillings. That is addition.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Whole Numbers (10.
2. Explain Whole Numbers (10 to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Try this activity: share tasks in identifying place value of numbers up to tens of thousands using place value apparatus and other resources,
4. Show that you can: use place value and total value of digits up to tens of thousands in daily life situations,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Whole Numbers (10. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: What should you consider when writing numbersin words?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Share tasks in identifying place value of numbers up to tens of thousands using place value apparatus and other resources,
2. Read numbers up to10,000 in symbols,
3. Team up with peers to read and write numbers up to 1,000 in words froma number chart or other resources,
4. Work with peers and arrange numbers up to 1,000 from smallest to largest and largest to smallest using number cards and share with others,
